subject.title: [Feature]: Support multi-target cron delivery from configured target sets

question: Should OpenClaw add a core multi-target cron delivery contract now, and should its initial scope be explicit per-job target lists only rather than persistent named target sets?
rationale: The request adds a public cron/protocol configuration surface and changes delivery, audit, idempotency, authorization, and session-state semantics across channels; the correct permanent contract cannot be selected safely from prior unmerged alternatives.

options.title: Sponsor explicit target-list delivery
options.body: Add a backward-compatible explicit target list with per-target results and safe destination-awareness reuse, while keeping named target sets out of the first implementation.

options.title: Sponsor target lists and named sets together
options.body: Define an operator-managed target-set configuration owner, lifecycle, authorization model, and upgrade contract before implementation.

options.title: Defer core support
options.body: Leave this as a tracked design request until the proactive-context and session-write safety contracts are settled further.

recommendation.title: Sponsor explicit target-list delivery
recommendation.body: Add a backward-compatible explicit target list with per-target results and safe destination-awareness reuse, while keeping named target sets out of the first implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The closest merged behavior is the destination-session delivery path this feature must extend without bypassing its safety model.
